page.layout: Running head top centre-left "DISTINCT. XIIII." with page number 227 at top right. Above the text, three lines of Greek with a continuing Latin line in roman. Then a decorative ornament. Then a centred heading, a subtitle, a chapter line "CAP. I." and the body, one column with marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text, the gathering mark "p.ij".

main_text.p: ἅγιον, πνεῦμα Θεοῦ, πνεῦμα ἀληθείας, ἀποστελλόμενον ὑπὸ Θεοῦ, ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς, ἀλλ' ἅγιον ἀγαθὸν ἡγεμονικὸν, πνεῦμα ζω- ποιὸν, qcc ni s, equ Filij nomen, neque generationis appellatione Spiritui sancto tribuam, vt idem Basilius Homil.1. de Sancto Baptismo praeclarè monet. Caeterum quum & de Filio, & de Spiritu sancto scriptura sacra vsurpat voces Procedit, exiit, venit, ad beneficium illud, quo vterque nobis donatus est à Patre potiùs, quàm ad arcanam illam processionis ineffabilis rationem explicandam pertinet. Quod iste nō vidit.
main_text.head: DISTINCTIO XIIII.
Quod gemina est processio Spiritus sancti, æterna & temporalis.
CAP. I.
main_text.p: Præterea diligenter adnotandum est, quòd gemina est processio Spiritus sancti: æterna videlicet, quæ ineffabilis est, quæ à Patre & Filio æternaliter & sine tempore processit: & temporalis, quæ à Patre & Filio ad sanctificandam creaturam procedit. Et sicut ab æterno communiter ac simul procedit à Patre & Filio: ita & in tempore communiter & simul ab utroque procedit ad creaturam, non divisim à Patre in Filium, & à Filio ad creaturam. Unde Aug. in 15. lib. de Tri. ait, Spiritus sanctus non de Patre procedit in Filium, & de Filio procedit ad sanctificandam creaturam: sed simul de utroque procedit, quanuis hoc Filio Pater dederit, ut sicut de se, ita etiam de illo procedat.Cap.27.De aeterna processione Spiritus sancti
Cap.27. De aeterna processione Spiritus sancti

page.notes: The Greek lines at the top are reproduced from a small, rough print and are uncertain in places. The marginal notes "Cap.27." and "De aeterna processione Spiritus sancti" stand in the right margin. The ornament between the sections is not text. The drop cap A/P at the start of the chapter is a decorative woodcut initial, transcribed as Præterea.
